result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers name the same concrete problems and fix them well: autosave with undo, a canonical stored unit, scoped resets moved to Advanced, and task-based grouping. B is a bit stronger on defaults and on shrinking the list, with copy-from-another-hive, a hive-level notification switch and search. A is clearly more honest that it can't know what causes the reviews, and it gives a fuller plan to check after release: tag reviews and tickets, check existing analytics, stage the rollout with named metrics. That outweighs B's edge. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers name the specific problem behaviours and propose autosave, removing the unit-change confirmation, safer scoped resets and grouped settings. A is a little stronger on defaults because it also offers copying alert settings from another hive. B is much better on uncertainty: it admits it hasn't seen the reviews, suggests tagging reviews and checking analytics before shipping, and proposes a staged rollout with specific metrics, including alert mute rate to catch noisy defaults.
